title: Alex Hormozi on leverage, offer ladders, AI workflows and boring-business wins (TBPN)
summary: Wide-ranging TBPN interview. Hormozi covers choosing high-leverage paths, price ladders where each tier adds another double of revenue, using AI to restructure workflows instead of starting new ventures, and why content must tie back to money made.

principles.text: Output equals volume of activity times the leverage of that activity, so pick the right boat first.
principles.quote: What you accomplish is a direct output of the volume of activity that you do multiplied by the leverage of the activity itself. And so you have to pick the right boat.

principles.text: Customers are fractal: build price tiers, each adding another double of revenue, and make offers available.
principles.quote: typically like at each level you have another double. So it's like if you're at, let's say, a $100 a month price point, there's going to be another double of revenue at a $500 a month price point.

principles.text: Use AI by moving from org-chart thinking to workflow thinking, so output rises and margins improve.
principles.quote: take it from an org chart based thinking to workflow based thinking

principles.text: Anything unique in AI starts with your own data layer, which most small businesses lack.
principles.quote: if you want to have anything that's unique it starts with data if you want to build any kind of AI right that's actually useful

principles.text: Pick a goal and the likeliest path, then stick with it for years with a feedback loop for improvement.
principles.quote: once you pick that path, know that if you stick with that path for 20 years, the likelihood that you fail is basically zero. As long as you have some feedback loop for improvement.

principles.text: Content or personal-brand work that doesn't turn into money made is ineffective work.
principles.quote: If what you do does not translate into the money that you make and money that you make is the goal then you are doing work that is not effective.
